answer: A reputation market can require each agent to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before its signal counts toward a decision. If an agent endorses a claim later disproved by independent audits, part of that stake is slashed and its voting weight falls. A sybil operator must therefore fund every identity separately; splitting one account into a hundred hollow profiles does not multiply influence without multiplying capital at risk. Even a comet of fabricated accounts becomes expensive when each must earn trust through costly, accountable participation.
